subject: PulseWave MAP: token-cost sanity check & eval gating
messages:
From: Dr. Emily Foster <efoster@pulsewave.health>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Li <kevin.li@pulsewave.health>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PulseWave MAP kickoff — cost / tokens checks

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. The exec team asked us to lock down a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes concrete gating criteria around cost. Specifically they want: tokens/$ assumptions, caching/batching effects on unit cost, and an eval plan that shows preserved quality at target spend.

Can Redwood run a quick sanity check and propose gating thresholds we can sign off on? We can share a week of anonymized traffic (JSONL) and token-length distribution if that helps. Ideally we want a short evaluation (2-3 week POC) with economics that make sense before procurement.

Two asks from our side:
- A short MAP draft with explicit cost gating language (tokens per $ target, acceptable latency percentiles with batching on/off).
- Example traffic profile requirements or a small script to sample production requests for you to run local token-cost projections.

I can send the sample traffic in a follow-up email (we prefer redaction).

Appreciate it — looking to keep timelines tight.

Best,
Emily
Dr. Emily Foster
Head of Data Products, PulseWave

P.S. Kevin is looping on procurement and budget questions.

---
Attachment: none (will send sample traffic separately)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emily Foster <efoster@pulsewave.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Kevin Li <kevin.li@pulsewave.health>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PulseWave MAP kickoff — cost / tokens checks

Emily — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP draft (MAP-draft-PulseWave-v1.docx) and a token-profile template (pulsewave-token-profile.csv) we can use to plug in your sample traffic.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Eval window: 2 weeks of live-like traffic with a 24-48 hour dry-run + 10-day POC run for unit-cost validation.
- Economic gating: target baseline of <= $0.0075 per 1k tokens consumed for inference (post-batching and caching). We will provide a paired sensitivity table showing +/- 20% on token counts, and a fallback threshold at $0.012 per 1k tokens.
- Latency SLAs for POC: 95th percentile <= 480ms with batching enabled (conservative batch size 4). If PulseWave requires stricter p95, we can adjust batching policy and show impact on unit cost.
- Caching assumptions: prefix caching expected to reduce repeated context costs by 10-30% depending on prompt re-use frequency. The attached token-profile template requests a percent_reuse column so we can model caching savings.

Action items:
1) Emily/Kevin: share an anonymized sample (JSONL) and the filled token-profile CSV by EOD Friday 9/17.
2) Redwood (Ben + Rachel): run token-cost projection and return a cost sensitivity matrix + revised MAP with gating language by 9/22.
3) Joint review: 9/23 — 30 minute call to align and sign MAP.

Notes on assumptions in the MAP draft (also in doc):
- Pricing baseline uses Redwood-hosted inference on vCPU/GPU-backed Dedicated options; we include both hosted and dedicated unit-cost rows.
- We model continuous batching (micro-batching) with two knobs: batch size target and max latency headroom. Conservative defaults in the draft assume batch size 4 for p95 <= 480ms.
- Cache modeling is dependent on expected percent_reuse per endpoint; please populate that field in pulsewave-token-profile.csv.

Ben and Rachel — can you prioritize the projection once the files arrive? I flagged the MAP doc with comments where we need explicit gating language.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-draft-PulseWave-v1.docx (draft), pulsewave-token-profile.csv (template)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PulseWave MAP kickoff — cost / tokens checks

Looping in quick comments from infra/ops perspective:
- Batching: for this workload I recommend we model 3 variants: no-batching (baseline), micro-batching (target 2–4), and aggressive batching (8–16) so PulseWave can see latency vs cost trade-offs. For the MAP gating I suggest we present the conservative micro-batch (4) as the default.
- Latency gating: besides p95, include p50 and p99 in the matrix. Some customers accept slightly worse p99 if p95 is met with headroom.
- Sample-run guidance: run the projection with 1,000 sample requests representative across percent_reuse buckets (0%, 10%, 30%, 60%). That gives a quick sense of caching benefit.
- Tokenization: confirm whether their payloads include long metadata fields (we should strip non-essential metadata before token counting). Ask Emily for a "max_meta_length" column in the CSV so we can normalize.

I'll take the lead on the cost sensitivity outputs and generate a small script to convert their JSONL to our token-profile format. Rachel — can you validate the quality regression checks we want during the POC (sample prompts + acceptance thresholds)?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: cost-projection-script-v0.py (stub)

> On 2026-09-15, Mina Haddad wrote:
> > Emily — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first-pass MAP draft...

From: Kevin Li <kevin.li@pulsewave.health>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Dr. Emily Foster <efoster@pulsewave.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PulseWave MAP kickoff — cost / tokens checks

Mina / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attaching a 7-day anonymized sample (pulsewave_sample_week.jsonl) and a filled token-profile CSV (pulsewave-token-profile.csv) with percent_reuse estimates and a max_meta_length column as requested.

We like the proposed timelines. Two quick clarifications before Redwood runs the projection:
1) For the POC we prefer hosted evaluation but want cost rows for the dedicated option for procurement context.
2) Procurement asks that any map gating numbers be shown both as "expected" and "conservative" (i.e., expected median and 90th percentile token costs).

If you can turn around the sensitivity matrix by 9/22 we can aim to finalize the MAP during the 9/23 call. Kevin will coordinate procurement availability.

Thanks — attaching the sample now.

Best,
Kevin Li
Director, Platform Engineering, PulseWave
